content.value_statement: Missing or weak browser headers expose web apps to common client-side attacks. This skill audits headers and gives implementation guidance for safer deployments.
actual_capabilities: Reviews HTTP response headers for missing or weak security controls.
Checks Content Security Policy, HSTS, CORS, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy settings.
Explains attack impact for XSS, clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and downgrade risks.
Provides implementation guidance for Express.js, Nginx, and Apache configurations.
Creates prioritized remediation plans and testing checklists for deployment teams.
limitations: It does not replace a full penetration test or application security review.
It needs accurate response headers or an authorized target URL to assess a site.
Generated configurations must be tested in staging before production use.
Example domains and commands must be adapted to the user environment.

use_cases.title: Review a Launch Checklist
use_cases.description: Assess whether a new web app has the essential browser security headers before release.

use_cases.title: Harden Existing Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Turn weak CSP, HSTS, and CORS settings into a prioritized remediation plan.

use_cases.title: Prepare Security Evidence
use_cases.description: Generate a readable header report for audits, vendor reviews, or internal risk tracking.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Header Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these HTTP response headers. Identify missing security headers, explain the risk, and list the top fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: CSP Improvement Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Content Security Policy. Find unsafe directives, explain browser impact, and suggest a safer staged rollout plan.

prompt_templates.title: CORS and HSTS Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these CORS and HSTS settings. Flag dangerous combinations and recommend settings for a production web application.

prompt_templates.title: Full Deployment Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a full security headers report for this application. Include severity, business impact, deployment risk, validation steps, and owner-ready remediation tasks.

output_examples.input: A web app has no Content Security Policy and no HSTS header.
output: Overall grade: high risk because browser-side protections are incomplete.
Top fixes: add HSTS after HTTPS validation, then deploy CSP in report-only mode.
Validation: confirm redirects, check browser console violations, and re-scan headers after deployment.

output_examples.input: An API returns wildcard CORS with credentials enabled.
output: Finding: wildcard CORS with credentials can expose authenticated data to untrusted origins.
Recommendation: allow only trusted origins and reject unexpected Origin values.
Deployment note: test partner integrations before enforcing the allowlist.

output_examples.input: A team needs a staged rollout for a strict Content Security Policy.
output: Start with report-only mode and collect violations for one week.
Replace unsafe inline scripts with nonces or hashes before enforcement.
Move to enforcement after critical user flows pass browser testing.

best_practices: Audit real response headers from the same environment that users access.
Roll out CSP and HSTS in stages with monitoring and rollback plans.
Re-test headers after proxy, CDN, framework, or authentication changes.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example domains or policies into production without review.
Do not use wildcard CORS with credentials for authenticated APIs.
Do not enforce a strict CSP before testing critical application flows.

faq.question: Can this skill scan a live website?
faq.answer: Yes, when the user provides an authorized target and the environment permits network access.

faq.question: Does it write configuration files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that a maintainer should review before applying.

faq.question: Which headers does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and CORS.

faq.question: Can it help with compliance reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce readable findings and remediation notes for security and compliance evidence.

faq.question: Will the recommendations work for every browser?
faq.answer: No. Browser support varies, so teams should test modern and required legacy browsers.

faq.question: Is this enough to secure a web application?
faq.answer: No. Security headers reduce browser risks, but they are only one part of application security.
